questions.question: Which 1975 film features a great white shark terrorising the town of Amity Island?
questions.fact: Directed by Steven Spielberg, it was the first summer blockbuster.

questions.question: What is the name of the coffee shop in the TV series Friends where the group hangs out?
questions.fact: The couch there was famously always free for the group.

questions.question: Which actress played the title role in the TV drama Miss Fisher’s Murder Mysteries?
questions.fact: The show is set in 1920s Melbourne.

questions.question: Which band had a hit with Bohemian Rhapsody in 1975?
questions.fact: It spent nine weeks at number one in the UK.

questions.question: Which singer is known as the Queen of Pop?
questions.fact: She has sold more than 300 million records worldwide.

questions.question: What is the name of the fictional sport played on broomsticks in Harry Potter?
questions.fact: The Golden Snitch is worth 150 points.

questions.question: What is the name of the famous rock formation in the Northern Territory, also known as Ayers Rock?
questions.fact: It is 348 metres high and sacred to the Anangu people.

questions.question: Which Australian state is home to the city of Adelaide?
questions.fact: Adelaide was founded in 1836 as a free settlement.

questions.question: Which Australian tree is the koala’s main food source?
questions.fact: Koalas eat mainly eucalyptus leaves, which are low in nutrients.

questions.question: In which year did World War II end?
Which desert covers much of northern Africa?
questions.fact: It is the largest hot desert in the world, about 9 million square kilometres.

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent by land area?
questions.fact: Australia is about 7.7 million square kilometres.

questions.question: What planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Its red colour comes from iron oxide, or rust, on its surface.

questions.question: How many legs does a spider have?
Which country is the largest producer of coffee in the world?
questions.fact: Brazil grows about a third of the world’s coffee.
